sections.heading: PQ Devnet-0 Status and Key Generation Failures
sections.summary: Devnet-0 broke when clients failed to pre-generate XMSS keys before the 4096-slot boundary, causing late attestations, a 55-slot reorg, and Geth refusing the deep reorg.
sections.body:
- Devnet-0 had a mix of LeanVM v0.15 and v0.16 clients, but this did not cause a consensus split as expected; the version difference was only an optimization.
- At approximately 04:00 UTC, the network reached the 4096-slot boundary requiring new XMSS key generation; some clients (notably Prysm) waited until the last slot to begin generating keys.
  - On devnet hardware with 625 keys per machine, key generation can take up to 2 hours, far exceeding the 12-second slot time.
  - Tom Wambsgans noted that for a single validator per machine it should be ~200ms even without caching; the problem is many validators on one machine all regenerating simultaneously.
- Late attestations caused a ~55-slot reorg that Geth refused to process (default max reorg depth is 32 slots).
  - Barnabas increased Geth's max reorg depth to effectively unlimited; the chain is slowly recovering.
  - Geth (Csaba) has PRs queued to make reorgs faster and may also increase the default depth limit.
- Toni Wahrstätter noted in chat that having a max reorg depth on ELs is a bug that should be fixed.
- XMSS has a `prepare` method to pre-cache the next subtree; Prysm and others are not yet using it but plan to.
- Lighthouse reported no issues — they pre-generated keys 256 epochs in advance.
- Barnabas asked all client teams to log key generation rates and timing to build confidence in per-client key handling capacity.
- Agreement: ~1 day is a reasonable timeline for all clients to fix key caching; Prysm (Manu), Lodestar (cayman), ethlambda (Mega) and Grandine (hangleang) confirmed in chat.
  - Lodestar has a separate range-sync bug preventing syncing through 0-block ranges; working on it.
  - Nimbus (Agnish) not on the call; will follow up async.

sections.heading: LeanVM v0.17 Update
sections.summary: LeanVM v0.17 switches from sidecar to FFI, adds 15% faster recursion, runtime CPU dispatch, and is a breaking change requiring a new devnet.
sections.body:
- LeanVM v0.17 key changes:
  - No longer a sidecar process; now uses FFI (statically compiled into client binaries), which most client teams preferred.
  - 15% faster recursion time.
  - Single binary with runtime dispatch for AVX2, AVX512, GFNI — dispatch happens once at aggregate function call, not per kernel.
  - More granular control over what to keep during aggregation (can selectively remove XMSS from already-aggregated data).
- Performance on Potuz's NUC 14 Pro (Intel Core Ultra 7): 2.2 seconds recursion on 4 cores with the other 4 cores idle; likely ~3 seconds under full load since these machines are power-limited.
- Additional optimization potential: an incoming STARK optimization is expected to give a further 15-20%; also possible to trade 15% bigger proofs for 7.5% faster proving.
  - Potuz and Kevaundray agreed not to make the STARK more complicated until the full setup (proving config + networking) is settled.
- Proof sizes currently 200-300 KB.
- v0.17 is a breaking change — incompatible with v0.16; requires all clients to update simultaneously, effectively requiring a new devnet.
  - Agreement: v0.17 targets pq-devnet-1, not the current devnet-0.
  - Barnabas created [pq-devnet-1 notes page](https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/pq-devnet-1).

sections.heading: Staking Contract Migration to sys-asm
sections.summary: The PQ staking system contract moved to the sys-asm repo via PR; where the XMSS verifier contract should live is still open.
sections.body:
- Ignacio opened a [PR in sys-asm](https://github.com/ethereum/sys-asm/pull/60) moving the PQ staking system contract there, alongside other system contracts.
- The system contract has a registration queue similar to existing contracts; it makes a static call to a separate contract for lean XMSS signature verification.
  - The XMSS verifier is written in Solidity and uses the Keccak opcode for all hash checks, making it efficient as EVM bytecode.
  - The verifier lives in a separate repo currently; whether to merge it into sys-asm is an open question raised by Matt.
- Toni asked why the XMSS verifier would be a separate contract rather than part of the pre-registration contract; Ignacio is open to consolidating.
- Formal verification of the EVM bytecode is possible using EVM formal semantics but is not a blocker for devnets.
- Follow-up: Ignacio to sync with Matt and Toni on contract placement; relevant Discord thread shared.

sections.heading: Key Derivation ERC and Mnemonic Reuse
sections.summary: An ERC specifying XMSS and VRF key derivation from mnemonics was presented; validators should not be forced to reuse their BLS mnemonic.
sections.body:
- Manu presented [ERC PR 2214](https://github.com/ethereum/ERCs/pull/2214) specifying how to derive XMSS and VRF seeds from a mnemonic, complementing the existing spec (which covers seed-to-leaf derivation but not mnemonic-to-seed).
  - Derivation path: mnemonic → account → validator child → lean XMSS key / VRF key.
- A separate ERC for JSON keystore format (analogous to ERC 2335 for BLS) is also planned by Manu but not yet started.
- Barnabas raised concern about mnemonic reuse: validators who burned or secured their BLS mnemonic may not be able to derive PQ keys from it.
  - Manu confirmed the current ERC ties a single mnemonic to both BLS and XMSS/VRF keys.
  - Kevaundray and Barnabas: validators should be able to use a different mnemonic for PQ keys, so the ERC should not make same-mnemonic usage mandatory; Manu is open to reconsidering. To continue async on the PR.
- Gottfried Herold noted that reusing the old mnemonic should still work safely (children cannot reveal siblings or parents), but agreed the ERC should account for both cases.
- Action: Gottfried to review the ERC for cryptographic soundness; further discussion async on the PR.

sections.heading: Staggered Aggregation Implementation Status
sections.summary: Only Silver (vlad) has implemented staggered aggregation; Barnabas wants it in a follow-up network, Potuz argued it would reduce chaos.
sections.body:
- Potuz asked whether staggered aggregation (aggregators releasing every 500ms, skipping broadcast if not adding many keys) has been implemented.
  - Reference commit: [consensus-specs commit 4595f0fc9](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/commit/4595f0fc9be7e3611f0187a2ff5fee00e120f751).
- Silver (vlad) confirmed they implemented it, sharing the [commit link](https://github.com/gattaca-com/pq-silver/commit/b32180007371b4cde166fd3c91de09a57117a0b9); timing logic is in `ticker.rs`.
- Prysm (Terence) confirmed it is not implemented; ethpandaops devnet doc lists staggered aggregators as not in pq-devnet-0.
- Barnabas recommended staggered aggregation for a follow-up network to avoid adding chaos to the already-broken devnet-0.
  - Potuz disagreed, noting it should reduce chaos, not add it.
- Kevaundray deferred the question of what goes into the next devnet until the current one is fixed.

sections.heading: Aggregator Role Design
sections.summary: A separate aggregator role with balance-weighted selection was discussed; the group decided to defer it and noted it could push the design toward PQ-DC.
sections.body:
- Kevaundray raised whether to define an explicit aggregator role in EIP-7870, potentially opt-in and restricted to staked entities above a threshold.
- Potuz explained the mechanics: aggregators would still be sampled randomly from a restricted set; it's not a DoS vector because selection is random and limited per subnet.
  - Selection could be balance-weighted to prevent Sybil attacks from low-stake entities.
  - Implementation could hack around fork changes (e.g., using a bit from the committed VRF or proof-of-possession key).
- Potuz cautioned that if this change affects issuance, rewards, and penalties, it pushes into territory where PQ-DC (instead of PQ-Gasper) would be more appropriate.
  - PQ-DC removes aggregation from the hot path of the slot, potentially avoiding the need for a separate aggregator role entirely.
  - Potuz believes the aggregator role will eventually be needed (for quick slots, faster finality) but prefers to avoid it in the first PQ fork.
- For head votes specifically (e.g., 512-member committees in PQ-DC), aggregation may not be needed at all — votes can be concatenated or referenced without inclusion in the block.
  - Francesco D'Amato confirmed the Lean spec already works without putting head votes in the block.
- Finality attestation aggregation is the part that actually needs an aggregator; Potuz suggested (in chat) that all attesters could serve as the aggregator role for finality; Francesco D'Amato noted finality aggregation has no hard deadline, it just adds to finality time.
- Decision deferred: the separate aggregator role is postponed; async discussion will continue on whether its complexity tips the balance toward PQ-DC.

sections.heading: Networking Methodology and Seacast/Waggle Implementations
sections.summary: Seacast/Waggle work spans Kamil's Lighthouse branch, Csaba's Go (Prysm) implementation and vlad's in-progress Silver one; Kamil asked for a shared P2P spec.
sections.body:
- Csaba is drafting a networking methodology document covering principles, best practices, and specific configurations for benchmarking; expected tomorrow.
  - Pari's approach: validate simulations against devnets at 100/200/300 nodes, then extrapolate simulations to 1,000–10,000 nodes.
  - Action: Pari to review Csaba's document once released.
- Kamil (Lighthouse branch) reported on a Waggle-based fast proof broadcast protocol (only parts of seacast, by his own description):
  - [Protocol write-up](https://notes.ethereum.org/@kamilsa/rk_I4TMJme) and [Lighthouse branch](https://github.com/kamilsa/lighthouse/tree/leanvm-proof-broadcast).
  - Simulations with ~4,000 peers and 32K validators: Waggle+chunking yields 1.7 duplicate messages received vs. ~7 for gossipsub.
  - Current devnet-0 peak bandwidth observed at ~40 megabits up/down.
  - Branch is ready for Kurtosis testing with instructions available.
- Csaba has a Go implementation of seacast on top of Prysm, running on Kurtosis:
  - Implements seacast's gossipsub binding first (closest to existing code), now adding Waggle binding.
  - Expected compatible with Silver's implementation; ready for testing by end of day or tomorrow.
- Silver (vlad) is building a Rust seacast implementation based on Csaba's spec, targeting interop with Prysm.
- Kamil raised the need for a shared P2P specification covering message signing, signature transmission, and other details not specified by seacast itself.
  - Kevaundray suggested Kamil align his Lighthouse branch to interop with Csaba's and vlad's implementations (both built on Csaba's seacast spec); Kamil replied that a spec is needed first. To continue async.
- Barnabas and Csaba agreed that single-client testing should happen in Kurtosis first, with shared configs, before spinning up multi-client devnets.
  - Potuz disagreed for P2P specifically, noting separated nodes are needed to test networking properly.
- Barnabas asked whether seacast/Waggle changes could be made backward-compatible to roll out on devnet-0; Csaba noted the issue is not backward compatibility but the hidden costs of restarting from scratch.

sections.heading: Attestation and Proving Timing Measurements
sections.summary: Lighthouse's initial devnet-0 timing data showed attestations arriving up to 9 seconds into the slot, partly due to CPU targeting and batching bugs now fixed.
sections.body:
- Mark (ethDreamer) shared preliminary timing measurements from devnet-0 for attestations, committee proving, and aggregate merges.
- Attestations were arriving up to 9 seconds into the slot initially; Eitan explained two Lighthouse fixes:
  - CPU architecture targeting was wrong, causing ~2× slower signing.
  - Attestations were batched and sent only after all were signed, instead of streaming each as signed.
- Committee proving starts at ~4.5 seconds, well within the 6-second broadcast deadline at current sizes.
- Aggregates arrive across a wide window; initial merge was set at 8 seconds, with a second merge to catch late aggregates.
- Potuz raised the scheduling conflict: a validator proposing at slot S+2 while aggregating at slot S+1 competes for the prover.
  - Potuz's suggestion: simply drop the aggregate duty if you're proposing in the next slot.
- Mark will rerun the analysis after the Lighthouse fixes and LeanVM improvements to get updated numbers.
- On 8-core machines, signing is the bottleneck for attestation speed.
  - Csaba raised concerns about minimum hardware requirements; Oisin Kyne flagged that distributed validators (MPC hashing) need ~3 MB/s continuously for key generation, suggesting higher max ETH per key would help.

sections.heading: PQ Devnet-1 Scope and Fork Transition
sections.summary: Fork transition testing deferred from pq-devnet-1; next devnet will stay genesis-based while focusing on LeanVM v0.17 and staggered aggregation.
sections.body:
- Barnabas asked whether pq-devnet-1 should test the fork transition (deploying system contract, key pre-registration, then forking to PQ validators).
  - This would require significant tooling changes and two forks to go from pre-deployment to PQ validators (deploying the system contract itself needs no fork, per Potuz).
- Potuz and Mark argued against testing the fork transition now; the current priority is timing and performance, not contract mechanics.
- Agreement: pq-devnet-1 will continue launching from genesis, not test fork transitions.
- Barnabas noted that with only a Friday call, the next devnet likely could not launch until Monday; Kevaundray pointed out a devnet can launch without a call.

sections.heading: Call Cadence Reduction
sections.summary: The group agreed to cancel the Wednesday call and reduce from three PQCL calls per week to one or two, with more discussion moved async.
sections.body:
- Potuz questioned whether three calls per week are still needed now that the spec is coded and clients are implementing.
- Multiple participants (Terence, Francesco D'Amato, Potuz, hangleang) supported reducing to one or two calls per week.
- Potuz suggested moving PQ topics into the existing ACDT call to save an extra hour.
- Decision: the Wednesday (Nov 25) call is cancelled; Friday's call remains; further reduction to be evaluated next week.
- The call itself finished in ~1 hour instead of the scheduled 2 hours; Kevaundray encouraged keeping calls efficient and moving discussions async.
